paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: The average probing accuracy using different MLP variations. We indicate the size(s) of hidden layer(s) in square brackets.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the average probing accuracy differences (in percentage points) for two multilingual BERT models—mBERT (light blue) and XLM-R (dark blue)—across four different MLP (Multi-Layer Perceptron) configurations, as described in the paper "Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models." The horizontal axis displays the MLP architectures, labeled as: "hidden:[50], linear", "hidden:[], linear", "hidden:[100], ReLU", and "hidden:[50, 50], ReLU", indicating the size(s) of hidden layers and the activation function used. The vertical axis, labeled "% point difference," is scaled linearly from -0.2 to 0.2, with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. For each configuration, two bars are shown side-by-side, representing the respective model's performance relative to a baseline (likely the simplest configuration or an average). In the "hidden:[50], linear" setup, both models show negative differences, with mBERT at approximately -0.15 and XLM-R at around -0.05. In "hidden:[], linear", mBERT shows a small positive difference (~0.08), while XLM-R shows a larger positive difference (~0.18). For "hidden:[100], ReLU", mBERT has a slight negative difference (~-0.1), and XLM-R has a small positive difference (~0.05). In the "hidden:[50, 50], ReLU" configuration, both models show negative differences, with mBERT at approximately -0.15 and XLM-R at around -0.1. The bars are grouped by MLP configuration, with no stacking, and the legend in the top-right corner clearly distinguishes the two models by color. The chart does not sort the configurations by performance, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond their color coding.
